final_feedback: it was not enough time to do this survey properly and with quality.

Well overall, I thought the survey was easy to follow. Most of the SAST outputs were helpful, but some used technical terms or repeated information that made them harder to understand. I think adding more simple explanations or short code examples would make the guidance easier for people with basic programming knowledge.

1. Actionability varied significantly. Across the evaluated outputs, tools that provided concrete, inline code examples were far more actionable than tools that merely provided conceptual warnings.

2. For complex queries (e.g., Python SQL injection), reporting every single user-controlled dependency (depends on user-provided value [1]...[10]) added unnecessary clutter without improving developer comprehension. You can try to consolidate data-flow traces into a clear source-to-sink path which will be much more effective.

3. Tools generally provided accurate severity labels (error/high) but guidance often remained too broad or generic (e.g., advising against external strings in command execution without showing how to safely parameterize or allow-list arguments in Node.js spawn).

Now relating to the survey structure and usability, the evaluation criteria (Clarity, Severity Justification, Specificity, Actionability, and Completeness) are well-chosen and directly capture the key dimensions of developer-centric security tooling. Side-by-side code snippet and report layouts also made it straightforward to assess line/column precision against the underlying vulnerability.  Wish you the very best in your research!
Maybe a little bit more time would be better, but overall is very balanced.
I would have loved to see a wider range of vulnerabilities,especially ones which have made headlines in the recent past ,SQL injection was presented a couple of times.
